newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil steady, cold boosts sentiment.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil steady, cold boosts sentiment.

text.p: NWE fuel oil was steady on Monday morning, but traders expected prices to stay firm on cold temperatures and strong demand in Europe and the United States.
"If you look at prices, they are the highest they've ever been except during the Gulf War," a trader said.
Another added: "They are very high but it doesn't mean they can't go higher."
In 1990 high sulphur fuel oil cargoes peaked at $135 a tonne cif NWE while low sulphur touched a high of $153.50 fob NWE.
Traders were unclear if Italy would continue to buy cargoes for Dec, having picked up around 250,000 tonnes last week.
One trader said congestion in Italian ports, which has led to delays of three weeks in some cases, would limit how much more prompt oil they could buy.
Another said Italian stocks were comfortable and their buying was concentrated in the January period, adding: "It's odd that they continue to buy aggressively when the market is as high as it is."
High sulphur cargoes were in demand from U.S. buyers, with a Dec 3-5 Coryton loading still available. High sulphur barges rose $2 to trade at $117.50 fob ARA.
